letters.title: An envelope with your name on it
letters.preview: Look, actual mail. Sort of.
pages: Okay, yes, I built a whole post office to tell you something I could have texted. That is exactly the level of sensible you should expect from me.
I wanted one place where a message could wait for you, without a blue tick or a reply deadline. Open it after a messy day, or three random Tuesdays from now. Nothing here is checking attendance.
[ADD A SMALL, REAL MEMORY THAT MAKES HER LAUGH.]
letters.ps: The stamp department is one person and the management is terrible.
letters.malayalam: ശരി, that's enough drama for one envelope.

letters.title: In defence of ordinary Tuesdays
letters.preview: An important, completely unofficial opinion.
pages: I think normal days are underrated. Everyone makes a big deal about birthdays and big milestones, but what about an average Tuesday where nothing exploded and you found a good snack?
This is an official letter saying you don't have to turn every week into a highlight reel. [ADD THE EVERYDAY THING SHE ALWAYS DOES THAT YOU ADMIRE.] Even on ordinary days, that's worth noticing.
letters.ps: You are not required to write back. This office has extremely relaxed rules.

letters.title: The fifth time? Suspicious.
letters.preview: There may be a reward for returning.
pages: Five visits? Either you're curious or you are checking whether I have fixed all my bugs. Both reasons are fair.
I kept this little note here because the best part of a place like this is coming back without needing an occasion. [ADD A TINY INSIDE JOKE ABOUT REPEATING SOMETHING.]
letters.ps: The unofficial loyalty scheme is one smile. Terms and conditions: none.

letters.title: A page from my notebook
letters.preview: One piece of paper, kept for later.
transcriptionPages: [ADD A PHOTO OR SCAN OF YOUR OWN HANDWRITING TO /assets/letters/.]
[REPLACE THIS WITH YOUR REAL HANDWRITTEN TEXT SO READ AS TEXT IS USEFUL.]
letters.ps: The placeholder artwork is intentionally not pretend handwriting.

letters.title: A letter for later-later
letters.preview: Sealed until its date arrives.
pages: Well, look at the calendar. The future arrived with absolutely no warning.
I hope you have collected a few good stories between then and now. [ADD A REAL REFERENCE TO SOMETHING SHE HOPES TO DO.] If plans changed, that's allowed too.
letters.ps: I wrote this earlier. I remain excellent at overthinking stationery.

letters.title: When your battery is at 3%
letters.preview: When everything has asked for a piece of your day.
pages: Have you tried turning the whole day off and on again? Kidding. Sort of.
You don’t need a clever comeback, a full to-do list, or a plan right now. Sit for a minute. Get some water. Find something soft to lean against. One thing can wait. Probably seven things.
[ADD HER FAVOURITE SMALL COMFORT—FOOD, SONG, OR HABIT.]
letters.ps: ശരി, that’s all from the very unofficial rest department.

letters.title: When you miss home
letters.preview: A small piece of Kerala in an envelope.
pages: Some places have an unfair ability to sit inside your chest, don’t they? A smell from the kitchen, a particular rain, or someone shouting from another room. Suddenly you’re somewhere else.

I can’t pack Kerala into a letter, unfortunately. International shipping would be a nightmare. But I can remind you of [ADD A SPECIFIC HOME MEMORY OR PLACE]. Missing a place and building a life elsewhere can both be true.
letters.ps: അയ്യോ, now I want proper snacks too.

letters.title: When you have great news
letters.preview: Yes, this calls for noise.
pages: First of all: WHAT. Tell me everything. I need the full version, including the unnecessary background details and the dramatic pause.
I hope you let yourself enjoy it before turning it into the next target. [ADD THE KIND OF GOOD NEWS YOU HOPE SHE GETS.] If this news deserves a snack, order the fancy one.
letters.ps: I will be accepting a full voice-note briefing.

letters.title: When something big is tomorrow
letters.preview: For the night before.
pages: The night before a big thing always makes ordinary objects look suspiciously important. Even the clock becomes a personal enemy.

You can be nervous and still turn up. Check what you need, set an alarm, and stop rehearsing every possible universe. [ADD A MEMORY OF HER HANDLING SOMETHING HARD.] One step at a time is a perfectly respectable plan.
letters.ps: ശരി. Tomorrow does not need a trailer tonight.

letters.title: When sleep is avoiding you
letters.preview: This letter has no bedtime lecture.
pages: If your brain has scheduled a surprise conference at 2 a.m., I would like to formally complain.

There is nothing you have to solve just because it got quiet. Maybe put the screen down after this, unclench your shoulders, or imagine us arguing about [ADD A RIDICULOUS SHARED TOPIC]. If you’re still awake, the night is just being slow; no need to fight the clock.
letters.ps: This post office is also terrible at keeping office hours.

letters.title: When your brain opens 47 tabs
letters.preview: The committee can adjourn now.
pages: I know, I know. What if this, what if that, and what if the other thing that has not happened and probably has no plans to.

You don’t have to decide the entire future from one uncomfortable moment. Write down the one thing you can actually do, and let the remaining tabs wait. [ADD A PRIVATE JOKE ABOUT HER OVERTHINKING IF SHE WOULD ENJOY IT.]
letters.ps: Minutes of the meeting: absolutely no decisions required.

letters.title: When you need a laugh
letters.preview: A low-budget comedy department.
pages: Breaking news: the Ministry of Unnecessary Drama has appointed you Head of Eye-Rolling. Salary: one imaginary jhumka and unlimited sarcasm.
A highly trained pigeon has been sent to deliver this letter. It got distracted by a samosa and is currently negotiating compensation. [REPLACE WITH YOUR ACTUAL INSIDE JOKE.]
letters.ps: Please do not report this office to management. I am management.

letters.title: When you feel stuck
letters.preview: No motivational poster inside.
pages: People love saying “just take the next step.” Very helpful, thank you, mysterious poster on the internet.

Maybe you don’t know what the next step is yet. That’s fine. Try a small experiment, ask one person, or just leave the question on the table for a little while. [ADD A TIME SHE FIGURED OUT A DETOUR.] Not every pause is a failure.
letters.ps: If anyone says “hustle harder,” I will hide their calendar.

letters.title: When you finish something big
letters.preview: Please accept this extremely official applause.
pages: Hold on. You finished it? That deserves a proper moment. Not the “okay, what next?” version. The actual sit-back-and-look-at-it version.
I wish I could hand you a ridiculous certificate with [ADD HER FUNNIEST NICKNAME]. Since I cannot, this letter must do. I’m glad you saw it through, whatever the road there looked like.
letters.ps: Certificate pending. Printer has gone for tea.

letters.title: When it is raining
letters.preview: A weather report from someone unqualified.
pages: Some rain asks for a window seat and absolutely no important plans. Other rain soaks your shoes and ruins your hair. Both have excellent dramatic timing.
If you can, steal a quiet minute and listen to it. Then remember [ADD A MONSOON MEMORY OR A KERALA PLACE]. It doesn’t have to mean anything profound. Rain can just be rain.
letters.ps: ചായ? This letter votes yes, but the kettle has its own opinion.

letters.title: When it is your birthday
letters.preview: An extremely unofficial birthday dispatch.
pages: Happy birthday! I considered writing something mature and dignified. Then I remembered who would be reading it.

I hope today gives you at least one moment that feels completely yours. [ADD HER BIRTHDAY TRADITION OR A FUNNY PAST BIRTHDAY MEMORY.] Whatever the year ahead brings, I hope you get room to choose things you like.
letters.ps: Age is classified information. Enquiries will be ignored.

letters.title: When you post your first vlog
letters.preview: The director has entered the chat.
pages: You actually pressed publish. I’m impressed and also ready to be insufferably supportive.

Please send me the link before I start pretending to be your PR manager. [ADD THE TRAVEL PLACE OR FIRST VIDEO IDEA YOU TWO DISCUSSED.] The first version doesn’t have to look like the hundredth. You made a thing and put it out there.
letters.ps: Autographs will be collected in the lobby.

letters.title: When you forget who you are
letters.preview: A few facts, not a pep talk.
pages: I won’t write a dramatic list claiming to know every version of you. People change. That’s the whole point.

But I do remember [ADD A REAL EXAMPLE OF HER KINDNESS], [ADD SOMETHING SHE FINDS HILARIOUS], and how you handled [ADD A SMALL TRUE MOMENT]. Those happened. They count. You can take your time figuring out the rest.
letters.ps: No inspirational background music was harmed in this letter.

letters.title: When you miss me
letters.preview: A suspiciously convenient envelope.
pages: Excuse me? You miss me? I’ll need this statement in writing, signed and witnessed.

Jokes aside, I miss the silly little conversations—the ones that start nowhere and somehow take twenty minutes. [ADD A REAL MEMORY FROM A CALL OR AN OLD DAY IN BANGALORE.] If you want to send a message, send one. No perfect opening line needed.
letters.ps: ശരി, enough. My ego has already grown three sizes.

letters.title: For a big day
letters.preview: A small note, exactly when it belongs here.
pages: A quick note before a big day: put the useful things where you can find them. Charge your phone. Drink some water. Ask what you need to ask.
You don’t have to make the day meaningful or brave or anything with a dramatic soundtrack. Just take it as it comes, one ordinary step at a time. [ADD ONE TRUE, GENTLE LINE YOU WOULD SAY TO HER.]
letters.ps: You can open this again tomorrow. Or not. No attendance register.
